real_work_title: Origen, Commentarii in epistulam ad Romanos (survives complete only in Rufinus's Latin translation; Greek original lost for Book VII apart from catena fragments not held locally)
urn_or_ref_inconsistencies: Work id suffix '_grc' but the work survives in full only in Rufinus's LATIN; both passages carry ENGLISH summaries, not ancient text in any language.

cts_urn 'urn:cts:greekLit:tlg2042.tlg012' is work-level only (no passage component) and unverified: local TLG XML confirms tlg2042.tlg008 = De Oratione; no evidence that tlg012 = Commentarii in Romanos [undetermined]. A greekLit URN is in any case inappropriate for the Latin Rufinus text; no CTS edition of the Latin Comm. Rom. known on Scaife -> correct_urn: none.

canonical_ref 'Commentary on Romans VII.16' does not match the SC 543 / Hammond Bammel chapter numbering, where the Rom 9:14-19 / Pharaoh material is Book VII caput 14 (SC 543 caput 16 covers Rom 9:22-26). 'VII.16' is presumably an older chapter division [undetermined].
Both passages share identical canonical_ref and sequence_number 16 despite covering different sub-sections.
Exact duplicate texts exist under sibling work 'work_origen_commentary_romans_eng' (passage_ids 06e8989f-778c-5ab1-8e7f-f46e60a6bcfa, 60c247a1-3164-51e8-ba8e-f9323de2fdd7).

The Latin 'quotes' embedded in the English summaries ('Non enim Deus indurat cor Pharaonis... permittit ut ipse se induret peccando', sun/occasio analogy, 'fingere sibi ex adverso personam... ad destruendum liberum arbitrium') are NOT found in the SC 543 (= Hammond Bammel) critical text of any of the 10 books -> likely fabricated/loose reconstructions; the sun analogy actually belongs to De Principiis III.1 ('sol ceram quidem soluit, limum uero arefacit', SC 268).
